behavior: A review signed by a model outside the pool cannot be archived, and the refusal names both the reviewer found and the models allowed, so the mismatch is diagnosable without reading source
Any pool entry may sign, not only the launcher's primary — the array is an allow-list whose first element merely carries the extra meaning of being the default
An absent pool skips the check so dotf still works in repos that have none, while a pool that exists but cannot be read refuses rather than silently degrading to no gate

Membership is exact on the trimmed id: padding is forgiven, but a near-miss id that merely resembles a pool entry is refused, since tool names cannot carry the guarantee when one tool serves several providers
The declared escape still works, so the gate is a gate and not a wall
The launcher pins provider and model explicitly instead of inheriting a runner default, and refuses a pool entry that does not carry what its runner needs
Every reviewer runs through the secrets facade, asks for a machine-readable stream, and gets a deadline longer than the runner's own default
The launcher defaults to the pool's primary, reaches any member on request so the fallback is exercisable on purpose, and refuses a model outside the pool before spending a review on it
Wrapped commands are shell-quoted so a prompt containing quotes, backticks or command substitution is passed to the reviewer rather than executed by the shell that re-parses it
The prompt names the exact reviewer id the gate will match and forbids editing the contract files, so a review cannot invalidate itself or be refused over a spelling
